About the IMAGINE Team

A global network of neuroscientists, physicists, and engineers collaborating to democratize MRI hardware education and development.

Contributors & Researchers

Below is the core research and development group behind the IMAGINE hardware plans and training resources, listed in CITATION.cff:

Dr. Udunna Anazodo

Lead Investigator & Neuroscientist McConnell Brain Imaging Centre, The Neuro (McGill University)

Dr. Anazodo leads the IMAGINE initiative. She is an Assistant Professor of Neurology and Neurosurgery at McGill University and Chairs CAMERA, focusing on making MRI technology globally accessible and sustainable, particularly for underserved populations in Sub-Saharan Africa and beyond.

Maureen Nayebare

Lead Researcher & Workshop Instructor McGill University / CAMERA

Maureen is a graduate researcher at McGill University, focusing on RF coil prototyping, low-field MRI hardware, and open science capacity building. She has successfully led multiple hands-on construction and training workshops across Montreal (MNI, Douglas, Polytechnique, MGH).

Marina Fernández-García

CAMERA Operations Manager & i3M Researcher Institute for Molecular Imaging and Instrumentation (i3M, UPV-CSIC)

Marina serves as the Operations Manager for CAMERA and is a PhD researcher at i3M in Valencia. She specializes in low-field portable MRI systems, permanent Halbach magnet array optimization, and global health capacity building.

Haile B. Kassahun

Electromagnetics & Gradient Optimization Engineer Mbarara University of Science and Technology (MUST)

Haile focuses on electromagnetics and gradient former optimization for low-field portable scanners, developing advanced CAD models and implementing mathematical design patterns like the discrete wire method.

Guillermo Sahonero-Alvarez

MR Physics & Systems Integration Developer Institute for Biological and Medical Engineering, Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile

Guillermo is an MR physics developer focusing on the MaRCoS open-source console integration, sequence programming, low-field image reconstruction, and machine learning methods for portable MRI systems.

Sipan Hovsepian

Robotics & Automation Developer McConnell Brain Imaging Centre, The Neuro (McGill University)

Sipan is an automation developer at McGill, having designed the three-axis automated magnetic field mapping robot (Field Mapper Robot) used for B0 magnetic field homogenization, calibration, and shimming.

Timon Machtelinckx

Magnetics & Gradient Coil Designer CAMERA Collaborator

Timon is a researcher specializing in magnetics and optimization. He developed the genetic algorithm models used for permanent Halbach magnet arrays and designed gradient coils optimized for low-field scanners.

Dr. Johnes Obungoloch

Senior Advisor & Head of Biomedical Engineering Mbarara University of Science and Technology (MUST), Uganda

Dr. Obungoloch is the Head of the Department of Biomedical Engineering at MUST and a senior advisor for CAMERA. He has co-led on-site educational workshops in Uganda, supporting hardware replication and training programs.

Stefan du Plessis

Biomedical Systems Coordinator CAMERA / South African Collaborators

Stefan coordinates low-field MRI development and training workshops in South Africa, overseeing on-site assembly, testing, and hardware verification for regional partner labs.

IMAGINE Project

An open-source preclinical MRI initiative of the Consortium for Advancement of MRI Education and Research in Africa (CAMERA). Sustaining diagnostic health equity globally.

Open Science Compliance

All hardware files are released under open-source hardware licenses. This project is developed to satisfy the requirements of the Open Source Imaging Initiative (OSI²).
